headline: The OpenAI Foundation has chosen 163 US nonprofits to share $50 million in grants to test AI in community services, arts and local news, EdTech Innovation Hub reports.
score_reason: Lowered 1 from the pool score 5: grantees were already being named on 2 Oct, and the results cited are the Foundation's own account.
importance_line: Community groups, local newsrooms and arts organisations get money to try AI without being tied to OpenAI's products, which matters first to them and the people they serve, but the funder is an AI company's foundation and the results cited are its own account.
summary: EdTech Innovation Hub reports that the OpenAI Foundation, OpenAI's philanthropic foundation, has selected 163 US nonprofits from 1,669 applicants to share $50 million from its 2026 People-First AI Fund, with unrestricted grants for work on community services, arts and culture and local journalism. The Foundation says the fund is not tied to OpenAI products, that recipients may use any AI tool or none, and that all grants will be paid by the end of 2026; some recipients were already being named on 2 Oct.
notes: Announcement date unconfirmed: the Local Media Association's selection was reported on 2 Oct (Editor and Publisher), so freshness is set to 2 Oct; change to NEW if the Foundation announced on 5 Oct. Read EdTech Innovation Hub in full; Foundation statements relayed as the article gives them.
